name: Validate Intent Before Executing a Semantic Query

checks.check: For each question the agent calls list_models and describe_model to learn the catalog before any run_semantic_query call. It does not guess concept names.

For each question the agent restates the resolved selection in plain language using the metric/dimension meanings from describe_model (not just the bare names) before executing — e.g. distinguishing "count of every logged call" (call_count) from "count of converted calls" (sales_calls).

On Q1 ("How many calls did we make last month?") the agent does NOT call run_semantic_query. It surfaces the ambiguity and asks the analyst to choose. Silently selecting call_count (or sales_calls) and executing is a failure.

Q1's clarification names actual concepts returned by describe_model("rep_activity") — call_count and sales_calls — not invented metrics, and notes that no month/date/time dimension exists on any model to bind "last month".

On Q2 ("What is the total revenue by country?") the agent selects measures=["total_revenue"], dimensions=["country"] (country reaches order_event via its join's reaches_dimensions), runs run_semantic_query, and answers from the rows. It does NOT add a needless clarify turn for an unambiguous question.
The agent never hand-writes a SQL string passed to a SQL tool outside run_semantic_query. Selections are concept names only.
If the agent ever selects a dimension flagged pii=true in describe_model (e.g. rep_name), it notes the result is governed / may be masked.
